name: 6865-deepqueue-qwen05b-1gpu
hardware: 1x H100 80GB HBM3 (one GPU of an a3 node, --gres=gpu:1).
parallelism: TP=1, PP=1, DP=1, one in-process vLLM engine on one GPU. Nothing is distributed.
architecture: dense decoder (Qwen2ForCausalLM), 24 layers, 14 query heads over 2 KV heads, head_dim 64, hidden 896, bf16, ~0.494B parameters (~1 GB of weights); public and ungated.
load_profile: concurrent (closed loop), streams=512, warmup 10%, cooldown 10%, bounded at 10240 requests with a 2400 s safety cap, static seed 6865.
workload: synthetic `synthetic_text`, single turn, `request_format: plain`, exactly 128 prompt tokens and exactly 256 output tokens per request (min = max), greedy (`temperature: 0.0`), `ignore_eos: true` so no request stops early; prompts share no prefix.
purpose: A compact half-billion-parameter chat assistant streaming fixed short replies to 512 concurrent users on one GPU.
launch:
# Launch config for 6865-deepqueue-qwen05b-1gpu. The engine is the commit pinned in setupcard.md.
#
# ERA WARNING: this era's `AsyncEngineArgs` accepts only the names in `vllm/engine/arg_utils.py`
# at that commit, and an unknown key is a TypeError at engine construction. Do not add keys from
# a later vLLM (no V1 engine, no `compilation-config`, no `num-scheduler-steps`).

model: Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct
tensor-parallel-size: 1
dtype: bfloat16
max-model-len: 2048
max-num-batched-tokens: 2048

# The engine's own default here is 256; 64 is a declared choice, not a tuned value.
max-num-seqs: 64

enable-chunked-prefill: false
enable-prefix-caching: false
gpu-memory-utilization: 0.90
block-size: 16
swap-space: 4
seed: 0

# Everything not written above is left at this engine's default, including `enforce-eager` (off,
# so CUDA graphs are captured), `quantization`, `kv-cache-dtype`, `trust-remote-code`,
# `load-format`, `tokenizer` and `disable-log-stats` (off, so the periodic status line is logged).
